clue.text: Sun always gets riotous darts coverage

indicators.note: coverage says the rearranged darts wraps around the other piece
riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters of darts are thrown into a new order

parts.note: ay is an old and poetic word for always

explanation.surface: The sun's heat makes a pub's darts players rowdy, and the papers always cover it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riotous' scrambles the darts and 'coverage' has the result wrap around 'always'; AY is a poetic word for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic name for the sun, the star that brings the day.

clue.text: Here they run from arboreal apes' leader?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from apes'

parts.note: arboreal means living up in the branches, read here as 'in tree'

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about where the apes running through the canopy came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arboreal' is read literally as IN TREE. Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National, where horses run.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous English racecourse, so a place where horses race.

clue.text: Arias from G&S supporting one from Trinity

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: the Holy Trinity is Father, Son and Holy Spirit; the Son is one of them
Gilbert and Sullivan, shortened to their initials

explanation.surface: Opera numbers by Gilbert and Sullivan backing a soloist from Trinity College.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue G&S 'supporting' SON puts GS beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arias are solo vocal pieces in opera, so they are a kind of tune to be sung.

clue.text: Greek, Roman or Hebrew flag

definitions.meaning: all three are peoples or tongues of the classical and biblical past
an archaic word for an ensign or banner, as in Shakespeare's ... Pistol, the standard-bearer

explanation.surface: A list of old civilisations, apparently asking which banner they fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is old and classical; the second is an obsolete term for a military standard.

clue.text: Wordy stanza Diddley penned?

indicators.note: penned means shut in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a stanza is a verse of a poem
Bo Diddley was an American rock and roll guitarist

explanation.surface: Asks whether a long-winded verse was written by the rock musician Bo Diddley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like 'written', but signals one piece enclosing the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe speech or writing that uses far more words than needed.

clue.text: Suggestion upset top mathematician

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint
a lid is a top on a jar or box

explanation.surface: A hint that offended a leading mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' reads as praise for the mathematician but is a lid; 'upset' in a down clue turns the hint word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of the Elements, among the most celebrated geometers ever.

clue.text: Blair type to play Hamlet? Hardly

indicators.note: to play suggests the letters of Blair type being played around with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone like Tony Blair taking the lead role in Hamlet? Unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' signals the anagram, and the definition is whoever would hardly be cast as Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor actor with a small part, the opposite of the leading role.

clue.text: Weird as quarks in certain hadrons

definitions.meaning: one flavour of quark found in kaons and other hadrons carries this name

explanation.surface: Physics comment that the particles inside some hadrons are odd.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday sense is odd; in particle physics it names one of the six quark flavours.

clue.text: Bad for everyone in butcher's whichever way we look

indicators.note: bad here means spoilt, so the letters of for are rearranged
in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: to butcher something is to mangle it, so butcher's gives mangles
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Meat that has gone off for everyone at the butcher's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' signals the anagram of 'for'; 'in' puts everyone inside the butcher's mangling, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for considering something from every possible viewpoint.

clue.text: Some separation anxiety for Judah's second son

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Suggests a biblical son suffered distress at being parted from his family.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this figure is the second son of Judah, brother of Er and Shelah.

clue.text: Parody scripture in accurate representation?

indicators.note: a representation re-presents something in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, the old school subject of scripture

explanation.surface: Asks whether a parody of the Bible can be a faithful picture of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here: RI joins ACCURATE and 'representation' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exaggerated imitations made to mock their subject.

clue.text: One stranded sailors thus hailed

indicators.note: hailed means called out, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a ship's sailors are its crew; so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A castaway being greeted by passing sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW + SO, said out loud, gives the castaway's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's Robinson was marooned on a desert island for years.

clue.text: Route zero comes west through American state

indicators.note: through says one piece passes inside the other

parts.note: Maine is a north-eastern US state

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west is reading right to left

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A road with no number heading west across a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes west' turns NIL into LIN, which goes 'through' MAINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief railway line or principal road between major places.

clue.text: Chaps when old discuss Jack's impulse buy

parts.note: 'old bean' is a dated British form of address for a chap
to talk is to discuss

explanation.surface: Old fellows chatting about a rash purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack swapped the family cow for magic beans, which grew into the giant plant he climbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale giant plant came from the beans Jack bought on a whim.

clue.text: Managed to get raise with share account

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word turns it to read from the bottom up

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: Someone who handled a pay rise and a share issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' looks like a pay rise but in a down clue lifts the managed word to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling a story or report, an account of events.

clue.text: Axes chopped up elm's woody tissue

parts.note: x and y are the two axes of a graph

indicators.note: chopped up means cut into pieces, so the letters of elm are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lumberjacks' axes cut up an elm tree's wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like the woodcutting tool, but here means the x and y axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical term for the water-carrying tissue that makes up wood.

clue.text: Songbird at maximum speed in Kent?

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light, the highest speed possible
the lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A bird flying flat out over the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is not the English county but Superman's alter ego, Clark Kent; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Superman's everyday identity has this first name before his surname.

clue.text: Wyoming place keeps top grade butter in lounge

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside another

parts.note: to lie is to lounge about
A is the top grade in exams
a ram butts with its head

explanation.surface: A Wyoming town keeping its best butter in the sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but something that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in south-eastern Wyoming, home of its state university.

clue.text: Third-rate actor and writer encompass Mjölnir's work

parts.note: a ham is an over-acting performer
a setter calls themself me, the writer of the clue
to ring something is to encircle it

explanation.surface: A bad actor and author surrounding the job done by Thor's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Mjölnir is the hammer of the Norse god Thor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor's weapon is a hammer, so its work is pounding blows.

clue.text: Mum on floor lags hot brewing vessel

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece on another sits above it

parts.note: ma is a word for mother

indicators.note: to lag is to wrap in insulation, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: to floor someone is to stun them
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Mother insulating hot pipes on the floor round a brewing tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lags' has STUN wrapped round H, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: The vat in which malt is steeped in hot water in beer-making.

clue.text: EU bloke in news is architect

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside another

parts.note: read as new's plural: N for new, twice
the European Union, as written
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A European Union official making the news turns out to be an architect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as more than one N, the abbreviation for new. Balthasar Neumann was a German Baroque architect.
explanation.definitionFit: Balthasar Neumann designed the Würzburg Residence, a famous building designer.

clue.text: Make verbal attack greeting racecourse spy

parts.note: hi is a greeting
a tout spies on racehorses in training to sell tips

explanation.surface: A tipster at the races hurling abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for criticising someone vigorously and angrily.

clue.text: Apprehensive about many a Berkshire town

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number
Reading is a large town in Berkshire, west of London

explanation.surface: Nervous about a visit to a commuter town west of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearing something ahead is anxiety over it, an equivalent phrase.

clue.text: Something expressed or deposited in some amount

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a sum is an amount
to put something is to deposit it

explanation.surface: Banking talk: a sum expressed or paid in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressed' means squeezed out, here coughed up, not stated.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm coughed up from the lungs is pushed out of the body.

clue.text: Having advantage over storm god produces surprise result

parts.note: a team up on its rivals is ahead of them
Set is the Egyptian god of storms and chaos

explanation.surface: A team ahead of a weather deity produces a shock victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting term for an unexpected defeat of the favourite.

clue.text: God's 'power in unbridled emotion' (NT)

definitions.note: read as God is, so an adjective describing God

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another
unbridled means unrestrained, so the letters run free into a new order

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
the New Testament, abbreviated as in the clue

explanation.surface: A quotation about divine might, apparently referenced to the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: '(NT)' looks like a scripture reference tag but supplies the final letters. 'God's' is read as 'God is', so the definition is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: All-powerful, the attribute of the deity.

clue.text: Devil's daughter inspires a Welsh name

indicators.note: inspires is read as breathes in, so one piece takes another inside

parts.note: in Milton's Paradise Lost, Sin is Satan's daughter

explanation.surface: The Devil's offspring prompts a name from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' means draws in, so SIN takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh girl's first name, the Welsh form of Jane.

clue.text: Catcher stops crooked playwright

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so one piece fills a gap inside the other

parts.note: bent means crooked, dishonest
a net catches things

explanation.surface: A police catcher stops a corrupt dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Bennett is the English writer of The History Boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Bennett is an English dramatist, a writer of plays.

clue.text: Uranium, nickel and tin good, becoming one

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A list of metals and a verdict that they are good, merging into a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining together as a single whole is coming together in unity.
